channel.title: 重生两万年 English
channel.description: 重生两万年的个人博客，记录文章、阅读和长期项目。

item.title: Why I Understand AI Governance as a Closure Problem
item.description: I have become less willing to describe AI governance mainly as a problem of principles.

item.title: What It Would Take to Implement T-ACL
item.description: If T-ACL stays inside a paper, it looks like a formal system.

item.title: Small Claims, Clear Edges
item.description: A writing note on making an argument narrow enough to inspect.

item.title: How T-ACL Differs from Existing AI Governance Frameworks
item.description: I do not want to present T-ACL as a replacement for everything that already exists.

item.title: Revision Without Drama
item.description: A note on keeping old versions visible without treating them as monuments.

item.title: What T-ACL Is Not: Misunderstandings About Closure in AI Governance
item.description: When a new framework is proposed, the first thing readers usually do is not understand it. They classify it.

item.title: AI Governance Does Not Just Need More Audits. It Needs a Way to Decide When a Case Is Closed.
item.description: AI governance is no longer short on documents.

item.title: What Does "Risk Under Control" Actually Mean?
item.description: I have seen one phrase in too many governance documents: the risks are generally under control.

item.title: A Tool Is Never Just a Tool
item.description: Notes on release choices, habits, and the quiet politics of software.

item.title: Not Every "Failure" Means the Same Thing
item.description: There is a word in AI governance that does too much work: failure.

item.title: Accuracy Is Not the Last Question
item.description: I have become increasingly suspicious of the question that often sounds the most reasonable in AI governance: how accurate is the model?

item.title: The Three Governance Failures: Premature Acceptance, Premature Rejection, and Indefinite Delay
item.description: AI governance discussions often focus on model errors.

item.title: AI Audits Are Growing. But Who Decides When They Are Enough?
item.description: The AI governance conversation can no longer be reduced to the claim that systems are not being audited.

item.title: Why I Care About Closure in AI Governance
item.description: AI governance discussions often revolve around familiar terms: transparency, fairness, explainability, accountability, auditing, compliance, and risk manag
